papers.title: Counting multigeodesics and the Selberg-Delange method
papers.abstract: We study the counting function $\mathcal{P}^m(X,x)$ for $m$-multigeodesics of length at most $x$ on a compact hyperbolic surface $X$ where $m$ is a positive integer. Building on the Selberg-Delange method, originally developed for counting integers with exactly $m$ prime factors in the interval $[1,x]$, we prove a large $x$ asymptotic for $\mathcal{P}^m(X,x)$. We show that for fixed $m$ as $x\to\infty$ the asymptotic is independent of the surface, whereas for $\frac{m}{\log x}$ bounded away from zero, the asymptotic depends on an infinite Euler product over the lengths of primitive closed geodesics. We also study the distribution of the function $\omega_1$, defined on multigeodesics $\Gamma$ as $\omega_1(\Gamma)=k-1$ for $\Gamma=(\gamma_1,...,\gamma_k)$ a $k$-multigeodesic. We show that as $x\to\infty$, the distribution of $\omega_1$ in the set of multigeodesics of length $\leq x$ is close to that of a Poisson random variable with parameter $\log x$. Both of these theorems rely on studying the generating function of the random variable $\omega_1$ which we relate to the Selberg zeta function.

papers.title: Spectral Convergence of Sparse Bipartite Graphs via the Line-Graphon
papers.abstract: Pure point spectral convergence is generally unavailable for sparse graph sequences, where Laplacian eigenvalues may remain unstable under graph growth. This poses challenges for analyzing spectral operators underlying many graph-based learning methods, including graph neural networks. We identify a class of sparse bipartite graph sequences for which eigenvalue-level spectral convergence can be recovered. Focusing on graphs with strong degree heterogeneity, we exploit the convergence properties of their line-graph sequences. Using a spectral correspondence between bipartite graph Laplacians and line-graph adjacency operators, we transfer convergence guarantees from dense line-graphs back to the original sparse graphs. This framework yields eigenvalue-level spectral convergence for a class of deterministic sparse graph sequences. We further analyze superlinear preferential attachment trees, establishing convergence to an infinite-dimensional limit operator. Numerical experiments empirically support our spectral convergence results.

papers.title: Spectral Regimes of Truncated sinc-Power and Pulse-Train Kernels: Edge Exponents, Per-Edge Plunges, and the Landau-Widom Limit
papers.abstract: A signal band-limited to one rectangular band and observed through a finite window is the classical concentration problem of Slepian, Landau, Pollak, and Widom. The eigenvalues of the operator cluster near one and near zero, separated by a transition called the plunge. The plunge width grows like the logarithm of the window length, with a universal coefficient of one over pi squared set by the band-edge jump. This paper follows the clusters and the plunge as the band is deformed. An elementwise power of the kernel smooths the band edge, and the plunge gives way to a power-law edge with exponent one less than the power. Disjoint copies of the band widen the plunge in proportion to the number of band edges, as the multiple-interval theorem of Landau and Widom implies, so the coefficient is a per-edge constant. Shrinking each band to a line gives the classical finite-rank operator. Overlapping bands give a multilevel staircase, and a self-similar band gives a cluster hierarchy governed by the Cantor dimension. At the smooth edge, rescaled eigenvalues do not collapse onto one curve. The edge descriptor passes from a constant to an exponent to an integer to a fractal dimension. For the single band, classical results place all eigenfilter zeros on the unit circle, with more of them inside the band as the order rises, so the dominant eigenvectors act as lowpass filters.
